correctness.rationale: Finite tree partition functions give exact root ratios r_n^F=F_lambda^n(lambda), r_n^E=F_lambda^n(0). Explicit derivatives at r_c yield doubled-map cubic coefficient \(C_b=(b+1)(b-1)^3/(6b^2)\)>0 and critical parameter slope \(a_b=(b-1)/b\). The inverse-square transform w=1/x² evolves as w_(j+1)=(1-2a_b t/n)w_j+2C_b+summable o(n) errors in the critical window. Uniform c(j+1)<=w_j<=C(j+1) bounds justify summation and give w_(floor(n/2))/n->C_b(1-e^{-a_b t})/(a_b t). Differentiation of r/(1+r) gives exact profile with parity. The standalone verifier checks 42 independent finite-tree rational ratios, 10 exact cubic identities and 48 finite-height (including both parities) asymptotic comparisons; finite checks do not prove limits.

value.rationale: Boundary sensitivity of a hard-core Gibbs tree is a natural quantitative probe of spatial mixing and the onset of nonuniqueness. The sharp coefficient and nonconstant scaling function across the entire \(1/n\) activity window are mathematically informative beyond the known critical activity and generic flip exponent; they distinguish criticality approached from above versus below, and provide benchmark normalization for finite-depth message-passing calculations. No universal theorem outside this family is needed for the precise finite-volume answer to be useful.
